name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap deliver a smooth, judder-free feel that suits Skyrim's exploration pace well. High textures look great on the Deck's 7-inch screen while FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers GPU headroom for stable 40 fps even in demanding outdoor areas.

profiles.Summary: Skyrim Special Edition runs well on the Steam Deck as a Verified title, with the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably handling its mid-range PC requirements at native or slightly reduced resolution. The game is a smooth fit for the Deck, capable of stable 40–60 fps depending on settings and area complexity.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's PC requirements, its Verified status, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capability. On your first run, check the frame rate in an outdoor area like Whiterun's plains — if it dips below your cap, lower Shadow Distance and Godrays first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load minimal; the 30 fps lock and 7 W TDP cap together maximize session length. Godrays and ambient occlusion are the biggest GPU costs in Skyrim SSE and are best disabled here.

KnownIssues: Mods installed via the in-game Creation Club or external tools may cause instability or crashes under Proton.
Some users report the intro video or launcher may need to be skipped or configured via launch options.
Outdoor areas with heavy foliage or distant terrain can cause frame dips compared to interiors.
Controller mapping works via Steam Input but the game's native partial controller support may require manual configuration for full button prompts.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native 1280x800 with no TDP cap lets the Deck run Skyrim SSE at its best visual quality; most interiors and towns will hit 60 fps, but dense outdoor areas with many NPCs or heavy weather may dip into the high 40s. Ambient Occlusion is left off as it costs significant GPU time for a subtle benefit at this screen size.

Optimal.Notes: A 45 Hz refresh and frame cap is the sweet spot on the OLED Deck — motion is noticeably smoother than 30 fps and the GPU stays comfortably loaded without thermal throttling. High textures look great on the OLED display and are largely free since they live in VRAM rather than stressing the GPU shader units.

profiles.Summary: Skyrim Special Edition runs well on the Steam Deck, benefiting from its age and moderate PC requirements that align closely with the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU capabilities. The game is Steam Deck Verified and ProtonDB reporters trend platinum, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience with minimal tweaking needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements relative to the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU and from general knowledge of Skyrim SE's engine characteristics. On your first run, check frame pacing in Whiterun and the Rift — those are the heaviest areas — and adjust shadow distance or Godrays if you see stutters.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU well within the 6 W TDP budget while remaining readable on the OLED panel. Dropping Godrays to None and disabling Ambient Occlusion are the biggest power savers in Skyrim SE.

KnownIssues: The in-game Creation Club menu and some mod-related UI elements may not scale perfectly to the 1280x800 screen.
Occasional stutters can occur when crossing cell boundaries in large open areas like Whiterun or the Rift.
The Bethesda launcher was retired but any leftover launcher prompts may require dismissal on first launch.
Some users report the game defaults to a low-quality windowed mode on first boot — setting fullscreen in the ini or in-game menu is recommended.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Skyrim SE's engine is old enough that the Deck can push native 1280x800 at high-to-ultra settings without FSR, though dense forested areas and large cities like Whiterun may dip toward 45 fps. Ultra Shadows are the most expensive single setting — drop them to High if you see sustained dips below 50 fps.
